title: Basic literals: numbers, strings and characters

quiz.explain: '1' is a char with character code 49. A char plus an int is arithmetic on the code: 49 + 1 = 50.
With a String on one side, + glues text together: "123" + 1 becomes "1231".
Underscores only make the literal easier to read. They are not part of the value, so println shows 17900000.
Double quotes make a String, and a String does not fit in a char: incompatible types. The empty string "" is valid.

quiz.q: Which is a valid character literal?
quiz.explain: A char literal is exactly one symbol in single quotes. 'AB' and '' do not compile; "x" is a String.

quiz.q: Which number literal does NOT compile?
quiz.explain: Underscores may only sit between digits. A trailing underscore gives "illegal underscore".

options: A string literal that contains digits
quiz.explain: Anything in double quotes is a String, also when it only holds digits. You cannot do arithmetic with it directly.

options: A value written straight into the code, like 42 or "Hi"
quiz.explain: A literal is a fixed value in the source code. The variable is the named container you usually put it in.

quiz.q: Do literals differ between Java 23 and Java 25?
options: Yes, char literals need double quotes in Java 25
No, they are the same; only IO.println for printing is new in Java 25
quiz.explain: Integer, char and string literals are identical in both versions. Java 25 adds IO.println and compact source files; use System.out.println on Hyperskill's JDK 23.

flashcards.back: A fixed value written straight into the code, such as 1000, 'A' or "Halsteren".
A whole number without a decimal point: 0, 10, -100.
Readability only. Java ignores them; the value is 1000000.

flashcards.front: Where may an underscore go in a number?

flashcards.back: Exactly one symbol in single quotes: 'A', '1', ' ', '$'.
A char holds exactly one symbol. Text with more symbols needs double quotes: "AB".
A sequence of characters in double quotes: "text", "123", even the empty "".
'A' is a char, "A" is a String. char c = "A"; does not compile.
'1' is a char with character code 49; 1 is an int.
"1231": with a String involved, + glues text.

flashcards.front: Do literals differ in Java 23 and Java 25?
flashcards.back: No. Only printing in a small program differs: IO.println is final in Java 25.
